description: Verifies the seal of a run. Short form, which needs only what is short: request is the run_trajectory request as it was sent, with its readout and its from, whose request has none, when it had them (the answer's inputs holds neither), and run_seal is the seal its answer gave. The run is computed again, under a physics permit and the limits and refusals of run_trajectory, and the answer is holds (the seal given is the seal the request runs to), cause ("run_seal" when it is not), recomputed_run_seal and recomputed_receipt_sha384 when it holds (else no seal: run_trajectory gives the true one), compared, and text_not_compared: no answer text the agent holds is compared. Long form: the whole run_trajectory answer sent back as it came, without request. Its state digest and run seal are recomputed from its exact hex values, then its request is computed again under a physics permit and the engine's answer compared with it, value by value and byte for byte, receipt included: holds is true only when every byte is the engine's, values_hold when every value is, else cause names the seal, load_signature (a signed load that does not verify), answer_text (with differs_at, the first field that differs) or engine_version (an answer of another version). A chain is verified by its request with from, run_seal and chain_seal, or by links, its answers in order, each computed again from the links before it; a chained answer alone is refused (AnswerCarriesNoRequest). Nothing is stored, so each form answers the same on every connection. On this open connection one address holds at most 1 physics permit at a time; a call that finds none is answered "Too many concurrent physics tasks." and nothing waits. An answer is waited for 60 seconds, and long work is stopped there.

inputSchema.description: Either request and run_seal alone, the short form: the run is computed again and its seal compared with run_seal. Or the whole run_trajectory answer sent back as it was returned, without request, the long form: held value by value and byte for byte, its signature verified first. Or links alone: a chain's answers in order. A chained answer alone is refused (AnswerCarriesNoRequest), and a compact answer sent whole (CompactAnswerNeedsRequest).

chain_seal.description: With request and run_seal: a chained answer's chain_seal.

inputs.description: The inputs of the run_trajectory answer, sent back as returned: the request that was run. It is hashed, and run again, with the answer's readout when it has one, under a physics permit and the limits of run_trajectory. A card's fields, units and bounds are in describe_card.

links.description: Alone: a chain's answers in order.

public_key.description: The base64 of the ML-DSA-87 public key (2,592 bytes) to verify the answer's signature with; without it, this engine's own.

request.description: With run_seal alone: the run_trajectory request as it was sent, with its readout and its from when it had them (the answer's inputs holds neither; the upstream request in that from goes without a readout, as run_trajectory took it). It is run again, under a physics permit and the limits of run_trajectory, and its seal is compared with run_seal. Its fields are run_trajectory's.

run_seal.description: The run_seal of the run_trajectory answer: with request, or as part of the whole answer.

seen_nonces.description: Nonces of signatures already seen: one of them again is SignatureNonceReplayed.
